defects.title: Receiving computes and exports the wrong weighted-average cost
defects.workflow: Stock receiving, inventory valuation, product cost, export
defects.preconditions: Audit-owned product has quantity 5 and average cost 80.25 KGS.
repro: Receive quantity 2 at unit cost 81.00 KGS for the audit-owned product.
Open the resulting movement and verify quantity 2 and total 162.00 KGS.
Open the product editor and inspect average cost.
Export products and inspect the product's purchase-price and average-cost columns.
defects.expected: Weighted average is (5 × 80.25 + 2 × 81.00) / 7 = 80.4642857 KGS, displayed/exported as 80.46 KGS at two decimals.
defects.actual: The product editor displays 80.75 KGS and the CSV exports 80.75 KGS in both purchase-price and average-cost columns. At quantity 7 this overstates value by 2.00 KGS.
defects.reproducibility: Confirmed in the post-receiving product UI and an independent read-only export.
defects.risk: Inventory valuation, gross-margin reporting, purchase-cost exports, and downstream financial decisions are wrong; error scales with quantity and additional receipts.
defects.acceptance: Use the full pre-receipt on-hand quantity and value in a transactional weighted-average calculation; round only at the defined persistence/display boundary; UI, movement-derived value, reports, and CSV agree for initial-stock and multi-receipt regression cases.

defects.title: Reports overview omits a completed in-range write-off after reload
defects.workflow: Inventory-loss reporting, audit reconciliation, and report export
defects.preconditions: A completed audit-owned write-off is documented on 2026-08-31. Reports is set to All stores with the default inclusive range 2026-08-02 through 2026-08-31.
repro: Complete the audit-owned write-off and verify the inventory movement/stock result.
Open /reports with All stores and the default date range ending 2026-08-31.
Inspect the Write-offs section.
Reload the report and inspect the section again.
defects.expected: The completed 2026-08-31 write-off appears in the in-range Write-offs table and its export; report totals reconcile to the movement journal.
defects.actual: Before and after reload, Reports says No write-offs and disables the Write-offs CSV export, even though the same overview reflects the audit product at zero stock on 2026-08-31. The selected end date is 2026-08-31 and store scope is All stores.
defects.reproducibility: Confirmed in two report captures, including a full reload, with identical date/store scope.
defects.risk: A core inventory-loss report can omit a real completed write-off, breaking operational and audit reconciliation and potentially understating shrinkage or expense reporting.
defects.acceptance: Every posted write-off appears immediately and after reload for an inclusive, timezone-correct date range and matching store scope; on-screen rows and CSV/XLSX exports reconcile by movement ID, quantity, value, store, and timestamp.

defects.title: Inventory movement table causes root-document horizontal overflow at desktop/tablet widths
defects.preconditions: Open a populated movement journal at widths 768–1440.
repro: Open /inventory/movements at 1440, 1024, and 768 widths.
Compare documentElement scrollWidth to clientWidth.
Physically scroll the root horizontally.
defects.expected: Wide table content scrolls only inside its table wrapper; application root remains viewport-width and navigation remains fixed in view.
defects.actual: Root overflow is 188 px at 1440, 604 px at 1024, and 844 px at 768. Root scrolling shifts the application shell/navigation. No root overflow occurs at 767 or 390.
defects.reproducibility: Independently reproduced across five widths with physical scroll probes.
defects.risk: Users can lose navigation and off-screen content; the page is materially broken across the md/table layout range.
defects.acceptance: Constrain the table/grid parent so horizontal overflow is internal at every breakpoint; document root has zero overflow at 768, 1024, and 1440; sidebar/navigation never pans.

defects.title: Transfer movement detail omits the destination inventory leg

repro: Post a one-unit transfer from Airport Store to Downtown Store.

defects.actual: Summary identifies both stores, but movement lines show only the source Airport Store -1 leg; the destination +1 leg is absent. Store balances were separately verified as correct.

defects.risk: Operators and auditors cannot reconcile both sides of a transfer from its detail page even though balances changed correctly.
defects.acceptance: Every transfer detail and print/export view shows exactly one balanced source leg and one balanced destination leg; totals and store balances reconcile.

defects.title: Customer-order creation accepts a zero-line, zero-total draft
defects.preconditions: Authenticated ADMIN opens the new customer-order form.
repro: Leave all optional customer fields empty.
Do not add any product line.
Submit the new-order form.
Open the created order detail.
defects.expected: Creation is blocked until the order has at least one valid product line with a positive quantity; no empty server record is created.
defects.actual: Production creates a Draft order with no customer, no product lines, subtotal 0.00 KGS, and total 0.00 KGS. Confirm is disabled only after the empty record exists.
defects.reproducibility: Confirmed by the before/after production screenshots; the created record is SO-000002 in the audit run.
defects.risk: Users can pollute order history and identifiers with structurally empty orders, complicating reporting, integrations, and operational reconciliation.
defects.acceptance: Client and server reject zero-line orders without creating a record; at least one active product/variant and positive quantity are required; regression asserts no sequence/record allocation on rejected submit.

defects.title: Cancelled customer order still exposes enabled tracking and confirmation controls
defects.workflow: Customer-order terminal-state enforcement and outbound communications
defects.preconditions: Authenticated ADMIN opens the audit order after its status is Cancelled.
repro: Open the cancelled order detail.
Inspect customer, tracking, and email/confirmation controls without activating any outbound action.
Compare disabled state across the terminal record.
defects.expected: A cancelled order is terminal: tracking fields and all save/send tracking or confirmation actions are disabled, and the server rejects equivalent mutations.
defects.actual: Customer fields are disabled, but tracking number/carrier/status/link fields remain enabled, as do Send tracking, Save tracking, and Send confirmation. No button was activated because it could send a message or mutate external state; server enforcement is unverified.
defects.reproducibility: Confirmed by a post-cancellation DOM/control-state capture at 1440×900; server mutation intentionally not attempted.
defects.risk: The UI invites invalid post-cancellation changes and outbound communication. If server guards match the UI, cancelled orders could be mutated or customer messages sent from a terminal record.
defects.acceptance: For Cancelled orders, disable every tracking field and save/send/confirmation action; API mutations fail closed with no tracking, status, audit-log, or outbound-message side effects; regression covers UI and direct API authorization/state guards.

defects.title: KKM queue terminates in a generic error with Fetch 403 responses at every viewport
defects.workflow: KKM connector pairing, fiscal receipt queue, and operational troubleshooting
defects.preconditions: Authenticated as the same ADMIN in the focused isolated reproduction; no fiscal action is performed.
repro: Open /pos/kkm at 1440×900, 1024×768, and 390×844 in the focused isolated ADMIN session.
Wait for the route to reach its terminal rendered state.
Observe the visible error banner and inspect the recorded Fetch responses for each viewport.
defects.expected: The authorized KKM page loads its connector and receipt-queue state, or presents a specific configuration/permission/service cause with an actionable resolution; routine rendering does not produce unexplained 403 responses.
defects.actual: At all three widths the terminal UI displays “Произошла ошибка” with only generic refresh/retry guidance. The capture records one Fetch 403 at 1440, one at 1024, and two at 390, without exposing the failed dependency or a setup/permission resolution.
defects.reproducibility: 3/3 focused viewports (1440×900, 1024×768, and 390×844); the route was terminal and not loading in every capture.
defects.risk: An operator cannot distinguish connector setup, authorization, or service failure, so KKM pairing and fiscal-queue troubleshooting are blocked behind an opaque retry loop.
defects.acceptance: For an authorized ADMIN, resolve the failing request or map each expected configuration/permission/service state to an explicit message and next action; identify the affected dependency instead of showing generic retry text; verify clean terminal behavior with no unexplained 403 at 1440, 1024, and 390 without requiring a fiscal action.

defects.title: Invalid dynamic IDs fail to terminate safely on multiple authenticated routes
defects.workflow: Authenticated deep links, invalid-resource handling, and mutation safety
defects.preconditions: Authenticated ADMIN opens the scanner's clearly nonexistent and malformed IDs for each supplied dynamic pattern.
repro: Open both a clearly nonexistent and malformed ID for each listed route pattern.
Wait through the recorded route settle interval and inspect terminal text, spinners, wrappers, and mutation controls.
Compare with the three negative-state patterns that passed: movement detail, movement print, and purchase-order detail.
defects.expected: Every unresolved/malformed ID ends in an explicit not-found or safe error state, stops loading, and exposes no enabled mutation controls or actionable editor shell.
defects.actual: Order, product, and store-hardware routes remained on loading states; inventory-count and store-compliance routes rendered actionable-looking editors, including Apply/Save controls; receiving, transfer, and write-off edit routes rendered edit wrappers/instructions rather than explicit not-found states. No mutation control was activated. Negative states for /inventory/movements/{id}, /inventory/movements/{id}/print, and /purchase-orders/{id} did terminate safely and are excluded from this defect.
defects.reproducibility: Nonexistent and malformed values were recorded for all 11 authenticated dynamic patterns. Eight patterns failed as described; three passed. Genuine valid-value coverage was only 1/11, so this finding is limited to negative-state behavior and is not an independent retest.
defects.risk: Users can be stranded on endless loaders or mistake unresolved resources for editable records; weak terminal-state handling increases accidental-action and support risk even though no internal stack/SQL/ORM detail was exposed.
defects.acceptance: Malformed and nonexistent IDs for every dynamic pattern return a deterministic terminal 404/not-found state; all edit/apply/save controls remain absent or disabled; loading stops; valid owned IDs continue to render; automated tests cover both negative forms for all 11 patterns.
